title: Rall (1959) passive 3/2 cable electrotonics coupled to a Morris-Lecar (1981) active dendritic Ca2+ spike hotspot for synaptic coincidence detection across Cuntz (2010) balancing factors (Pass 3 remediation table, Slot 058)
remediation_item: Couple passive Rall 3/2 electrotonic cable segments to active dendritic Ca2+ spike conductance equations to evaluate synaptic coincidence detection across varying Cuntz balancing factors.

passive_cable_constants.source: Roth & Häusser (2001) J. Physiol. 535(2):445-472, Table 2 (rat cerebellar Purkinje cell passive parameters from simultaneous somatic + dendritic patch-clamp fits); DOI 10.1111/j.1469-7793.2001.00445.x
passive_cable_constants.note: Values transcribed from memory of the published passive fits (Rm ~ 122 kOhm cm2, Ri ~ 115 Ohm cm, Cm ~ 0.77 uF/cm2) and NOT re-verified online in this offline pass; treat as order-of-magnitude Purkinje passive constants.

rall_cable_equations.dc_length_constant: lambda_DC(d) = sqrt( R_m * d / (4 * R_i) )  [Rall 1959 Exp. Neurol. 1:491-527, Eq. 2]
rall_cable_equations.ac_length_constant: lambda_f = lambda_DC * sqrt( 2 / (1 + sqrt(1 + (2*pi*f*tau_m)^2)) )  [Rall 1959; Koch 1999 Biophysics of Computation Ch. 2, Eq. 2.37]
rall_cable_equations.electrotonic_edge_length: X_e = l_e / lambda_f(d_e), with d_e the Rall 3/2 diameter of edge e
rall_cable_equations.path_attenuation_semi_infinite: A(tip -> hotspot) = exp( - sum_{e in path} X_e )  (semi-infinite equivalent-cylinder approximation; exact for Rall 3/2-matched trees seen from the soma, approximate centripetally)
rall_cable_equations.synaptic_frequency_note: f_syn = 1 / (2*pi*tau_syn) with alpha-function synaptic time constant tau_syn = 3.0 ms

active_ca_spike_hotspot.model: Morris-Lecar (1981) two-variable Ca2+ / K+ membrane: C dV/dt = -g_L (V-E_L) - g_Ca m_inf(V) (V-E_Ca) - g_K w (V-E_K) + I_syn(t);  dw/dt = phi (w_inf(V) - w) cosh((V-V3)/(2 V4));  m_inf = 0.5 (1 + tanh((V-V1)/V2));  w_inf = 0.5 (1 + tanh((V-V3)/V4))
active_ca_spike_hotspot.source: Morris & Lecar (1981) Biophys. J. 35(1):193-213, DOI 10.1016/S0006-3495(81)84782-0; Hopf (class II) parameter set as tabulated in Rinzel & Ermentrout (1998) 'Analysis of neural excitability and oscillations', in Methods in Neuronal Modeling (MIT Press) 2nd ed.
active_ca_spike_hotspot.biological_motivation: Llinás & Sugimori (1980) J. Physiol. 305:197-213 (DOI 10.1113/jphysiol.1980.sp013358): all-or-none dendritic Ca2+ spikes in Purkinje cell dendrites in vitro; Polsky, Mel & Schiller (2004) Nat. Neurosci. 7(6):621-627 (DOI 10.1038/nn1253): synaptic inputs on the same thin dendritic branch sum supralinearly (within-branch coincidence detection) while inputs on different branches sum linearly.
active_ca_spike_hotspot.note: Canonical Morris-Lecar barnacle-fibre parameterization (not a Purkinje P-type Ca2+ channel fit); the hotspot is treated as a single isopotential compartment at the lowest common ancestor (LCA) branch node of a synaptic tip pair. Residual: fit g_Ca/g_K kinetics to Llinás & Sugimori P-type spikes and resolve the hotspot as a multi-compartment active cable.

synaptic_input_protocol.waveform: I_i(t) = A_i * I_peak * ((t - t_i)/tau_syn) * exp(1 - (t - t_i)/tau_syn) for t >= t_i (alpha function)
synaptic_input_protocol.I_peak_note: Chosen so that a single attenuated alpha-input at the hotspot stays sub-threshold for every tip pair and every bf (single-input spike fraction = 0) while a coincident pair crosses the Ca2+ spike threshold for most pairs at bf = 0.2; this is a protocol choice, not an empirical value.
synaptic_input_protocol.pairing_rule: the 24 Euclidean nearest-neighbour terminal-tip pairs of the arbor (Polsky-Mel-Schiller within-branch vs between-branch protocol); hotspot compartment = lowest common ancestor branch node of the pair

coincidence_detection_predictions.linear_superposition_note: For a strictly linear passive membrane (g_Ca = 0 AND the K+ gate frozen at its resting value w_inf(E_L)) the coincident paired-input peak depolarization is exactly the sum of the two single-input peaks (superposition ratio = 1.0; gain = 2.0 for identical inputs; Lean 4 Theorem 5). The g_Ca = 0 ablation with a still voltage-dependent K+ gate is NOT linear and is reported separately. An active Ca2+ hotspot yields gain > 2 (supralinear) when the single input is sub-threshold and the pair crosses threshold.
coincidence_detection_predictions.same_branch_fraction_note: At bf = 1 (radial star) every tip attaches directly to the soma so the LCA of every tip pair is the root: same-branch fraction = 0 exactly.
coincidence_detection_predictions.predicted_sign_note: Higher bf shortens tip-to-soma paths but destroys shared sub-branches, pushing the LCA hotspot toward the soma and lengthening the tip-to-hotspot electrotonic distance; the predicted Pearson sign of coincidence window vs bf is negative (model prediction, not an empirical literature value).
